input: What has Salesforce changed in Agentforce pricing in 2026?

output.answer: In 2026 Salesforce made two major Agentforce pricing moves. Most recently, on September 3, 2026 it replaced its main cloud editions with new Core, Advanced and Max editions for Agentforce Sales, Service and Industries — $195, $395 and $550 per user/month respectively — each bundling a pool of Flex Credits for the whole org (500,000 / 1 million / 2.75 million per year) plus Slack, Tableau Next agentic analytics, security and Premier Success; Max keeps the Agentforce 1 Edition price (existing Agentforce 1 customers upgrade at no extra cost), while pricing on legacy editions is unchanged and new Agentforce Industry Edition pricing takes effect later this fall. Earlier, on June 25, 2026, Salesforce introduced outcome-based 'pay-per-resolution' pricing for its new Agentforce Help Agent — $2 per autonomously resolved service case, with no charge if the customer escalates to a human or walks away unhappy — generally available July 2026 and now listed as 'Help Agent Resolutions $2' on the official pricing page. These sit on top of the consumption models Salesforce added in May 2025 (Flex Credits at $500 per 100,000 credits, i.e. $0.10 per standard action / $0.15 per voice action, and $2 per conversation), whose rates were reconfirmed in the Flex Credits Rate Card updated April 21, 2026; Agentforce ARR has since grown to $1.2 billion in Q1 FY27 (May 27, 2026, +205% y/y) and past $1.5 billion in Q2 FY27 (Aug 26, 2026, +240% y/y).
caveats: The $2 pay-per-resolution price for the Help Agent comes from Salesforce's own pricing page and third-party coverage of the June 25, 2026 announcement; Salesforce has not published a dedicated press-release rate card for resolutions, so volume discounts or enterprise terms may differ.

Pricing and packaging are 'subject to change' per Salesforce's own announcement, and new Agentforce Industry Edition pricing was only 'later this fall' as of September 3, 2026 — it may have landed or changed since.

Third-party guides note a discrepancy in Max's included credits: the Agentforce pricing page says Agentforce 1 Editions include 2.5M Flex Credits while the Sept 3 announcement and Sales Cloud pricing page give Max 2.75M — confirm the number in your quote with an account executive.
From Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 26, 2026) the reported Agentforce ARR figure also counts Salesforce's other AI offerings, Slackbot and Headless 360, so it is not a pure Agentforce number.

passages.quote: Core Editions now include 500,000 Flex Credits, Advanced Editions include 1 million Flex Credits, and Max Editions include 2.75 million Flex Credits, giving customers immediate capacity to experiment, deploy, and scale AI agents across their workflows.

Core Editions: $195 per user/month (offering 70% more value than legacy Enterprise Edition); Advanced Editions: $395 per user/month ... Max Editions: $550 per user/month (zero pricing change and offering nearly 60% more value than Agentforce 1 Edition).

Agentforce Help Agent: Scale global service without scaling headcount. Autonomous agents engage customers on any channel, and Outcome-Based Pricing means you only pay when issues are resolved. Included in Advanced and Max Editions.

Salesforce explained its new pay-per-resolution pricing model, with businesses only charged when Help Agent resolves an issue autonomously. "If the customer asks for a human or walks away unhappy, there is no charge," Salesforce says. "Your cost is tied to outcomes, not activity." ... Pay-per-resolution pricing will be available July '26, Salesforce says.
Help Agent Resolutions $2 ... Flex Credits $500 per 100k Credits ... Conversations $2 per conversation ... Agentforce actions are 20 Flex Credits, while Agentforce Voice actions are 30 Flex Credits.

Each of these actions consumes just 20 Flex Credits ($0.10 per action) ... Flex Credits, available in packs of 100,000 credits ($500), empower companies to scale and manage AI investments effectively.

output.question: What has Salesforce changed in Agentforce pricing in 2026?

key_facts.fact: Salesforce launched new Core, Advanced and Max editions for Agentforce Sales, Service and Industries, bundling AI, Slack, Tableau Next agentic analytics, data security and Premier Success Plans into a single purchase.

New edition pricing: Core $195/user/month, Advanced $395/user/month, Max $550/user/month (billed annually); Max keeps the Agentforce 1 Edition price with existing Agentforce 1 customers upgraded at no extra cost; existing customer pricing on legacy editions remains unchanged.
Each edition tier carries an org-wide Flex Credit pool: Core 500,000, Advanced 1 million, Max 2.75 million credits; new Agentforce Industry Edition pricing takes effect later in fall 2026.

Salesforce announced pay-per-resolution (outcome-based) pricing for the new Agentforce Help Agent: charged only $2 when the agent autonomously resolves an issue start to finish; no charge if the customer escalates to a human or leaves unhappy; Data 360 and Agentforce unmetered during the interaction; generally available July 2026.

Salesforce's current Agentforce pricing page lists four meters: Flex Credits $500 per 100,000 credits ($0.10 per standard action, $0.15 per voice action), Conversations $2 each, Help Agent Resolutions $2 each, plus per-user licensing ($5 user license requiring Flex Credits, $125 unmetered add-ons, $150 Industries add-ons, Agentforce 1 Editions from $550).

Salesforce's Flex Credits Rate Card was updated April 21, 2026 with rates unchanged from the May 2025 introduction: 20 credits ($0.10) per standard agent action and 30 credits ($0.15) per voice action.

Agentforce annual recurring revenue passed $1.5 billion in Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 26, 2026), up over 240% year over year; from that quarter the figure also counts Slackbot and Headless 360. Q1 FY27 (May 27, 2026) had reported Agentforce ARR of $1.2 billion, up 205%.
